description: Calendar date of the observation, stored as text in YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS format (time is always 00:00:00 because records are daily). Covers 2024-01-01 to 2024-12-31 (366 distinct dates). The 488 supplied rows fall only in 1-25 January 2024; all other dates come from synthetic rows.
Stock-keeping unit identifier, format SKU + 4-digit number (SKU0001 to SKU0500). 500 distinct products with roughly 10 records each. Primary key together with date (no duplicate date/product pairs).

Product category: Apparel, Grocery, Electronics or HomeDecor. One category per product (normalised to the most frequent value in the supplied data). Share of products: Apparel 29.2%, Grocery 25.4%, Electronics 24.8%, HomeDecor 20.6%.
Season label derived from the calendar month: Winter = Dec-Feb; Summer = Mar-Jun; Monsoon = Jul-Sep; Festive = Oct-Nov. Used as a categorical feature in the forecasting model.

Units of the product in stock on the observation date (point-in-time snapshot, not a running balance). Integer, range 0-1,202. The latest record per product is treated as its current stock in the dashboard.

Replenishment trigger threshold in units: a product is flagged low-stock when stock_qty <= reorder_level. Integer, range 20-100. Constant per product (median of supplied values, or synthetically assigned where the product was absent from the supplied file).

Units sold on the observation date. Integer, range 1-83, mean 18.5. Target variable of the forecasting model and the demand proxy for reorder calculations. Synthetic rows include assumed uplifts (+20% Apr-Jun, +40% 20 Oct-5 Nov, +8% weekends); the supplied January rows average about 32 units versus about 17 for synthetic rows.

Procurement cost per unit, assumed to be in INR (currency not stated in the source). Float, constant per product, range about 26-24,889 (category ranges overlap). Commercially sensitive: the dashboard can hide this column via its Anonymise pricing toggle.
Supplier identifier, format SUP + 2-digit number (SUP01 to SUP30); 30 suppliers. Constant per product. Used in the Suppliers tab to aggregate lead time, low-stock products and reorder spend.

Supplier lead time: calendar days from placing an order to receiving stock. Positive integer, range 3-21. Constant per product. Used in target stock = average daily demand x lead_days x (1 + safety %).
